newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 16.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on January 16:
JERUSALEM - Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced down cabinet opponents into the early morning hours, securing an 11-7 endorsement of his new accord to withdraw troops from Hebron.
WASHINGTON - White House screening for guest lists at Democratic fundraisers' coffee meetings with President Clinton consisted simply of an identity check of birthdate and Social Security number.

WASHINGTON - Many presidential appointees are departing the Clinton Administration with sighs of relief, having served proudly in jobs they loved, but only too aware of the personal sacrifices required.
WASHINGTON - Defense Department police officers opened fire on four unarmed teenagers in a stolen minivan after a 10-minute chase that began in a Pentagon parking lot.

TBILISI, Georgia - Two tragedies occurred Jan. 3 when a Georgian diplomat's car skidded out of control and caused a violent five-car crash -- a teenager died and the diplomat's rising star was extinguished.
WASHINGTON - In retrospect, the University of the District of Columbia seems to have been built to fail, according to faculty members, former trustees and other educators.
